outline_action: ['Cite this study as the primary example of moving from human metagenomic association to experimental strain-level functional validation in the context of ICI.', 'Use the SagA/Nod2 mechanism to illustrate how specific bacterial molecules (rather than whole taxa) can be identified and validated as therapeutic adjuvants.', 'Contrast the engineered strain results (E. faecalis-sagA) with wild-type strains to highlight the importance of functional gene presence over taxonomic identity in predicting ICI response.', 'Note the limitation that validation is preclinical (mouse models) and that direct patient-strain-to-mouse transfer was not explicitly described, distinguishing this from culturomics studies that isolate patient-specific strains.']
remaining_gap: ['While this study validates Enterococcus strains, it does not validate other ICI-associated strains (e.g., Bifidobacterium, Akkermansia) identified in different human cohorts, leaving the broader landscape of strain-level validation incomplete.', 'The strains tested were human-commensal isolates (e.g., Com15) rather than strains directly isolated from specific ICI responder patients in a matched cohort-to-model transfer design.', 'Experimental validation is confined to mouse models; there is no direct experimental validation of these specific strain functions in human clinical trials within this material.']
